title: Actor-role components of dyadic event forecasts: exact attribution, near-collinearity, and a within-panel stability audit
description: Public artifact and L0-L2 verification release for the actor-role attribution contract of the accompanying manuscript, with a within-panel stability audit. The contract fixes feature ownership, unit and sign before results and makes every logistic forecast carry an exact group-additive decomposition into source-role, target-role, dyad and non-actor groups. It is a design convention and audit, not a new estimator (the decomposition is the logistic identity and coincides with linear SHAP under a training-mean background). The release is one paper path, not a reusable framework, and is executable at L0-L2 only. Includes the pre-registered one-shot unit-fresh 20% dyad-holdout evaluation (retrospective, not time-fresh), aggregate results, and an illustrative world-line preview. The within-panel stability audit is provisional, holdout-row-excluded and based on 50 dyad-cluster bootstrap refits; the public experiment scripts are a five-seed preview and do not regenerate those aggregates, and the restricted 50-refit audit code is not redistributed. ICEWS data, row-level predictions and labels are not redistributed. No general claim is made about graph features, persistence or any corpus beyond this panel. Source code is MIT-licensed; ICEWS-derived aggregate results are not MIT and remain under the ICEWS research-and-teaching terms. This is a v0.1.1 release candidate; the v0.1.1 git tag and DOI are pending.
notes: Source code: MIT, code only. ICEWS-derived aggregate results: research and teaching only, not MIT; see NOTICE and results/README.md.
